object_description: bridge-like school building with covered central square
design_condition: The building is positioned between the urban district and agricultural fields, using topography, trees, covered thresholds, and distinct outdoor spaces to mediate between them.

positive.statement: The precise volumetry is well related to the urban context.
The landscape proposal enhances existing topography and trees while engaging with neighboring buildings.
The placement generates three distinct and high-quality outdoor spaces.
Ground-floor public uses provide numerous independent accesses and facilitate sector separation.
The program distribution has well-proportioned circulation spaces with natural light and exterior views.
The bridge building establishes a dialogue between the city and the agricultural landscape.
The covered central square creates a generous meeting space for school and civic uses.
The park-school concept allows freedom of use, creativity, and sociability.
The relationship between interior and exterior is poetic and generous.
Integrating the sports program into the school building improves the organization.

negative.statement: The detached sports hall weakens the project's strongest quality and should be reconsidered.
The pavilions forming a border with the agricultural area penalize the landscape concept.
The retention of much of the existing topography is questioned under the site's constraints.
The number and size of stairs serving classrooms are insufficient.
The off-axis skylights create excessive contractions in the corridors.
Some rooms are blind or receive too little natural light.
The lower-ground-floor distribution, auditorium access, and stage relationship require improvement.
The basement corridor to the triple room is excessively long and poor in quality.
The facade passageways require more detail concerning climbing plants.
The cultural program raises questions about access, coexistence, and visibility.
The southern circus space is too disconnected from the cultural program.
Grass cover under the building will be difficult to maintain.
The energy concept remains incomplete and information on materials, ventilation, and green roofs is lacking.
The balconies and greening do not sufficiently prevent summer overheating.
The fully glazed lower and upper floors may create summer overheating problems.
The southwest facade is exposed to road noise and should accommodate less noise-sensitive uses.
The main entrance is cramped and disproportionate to the building's length.
Long corridors weaken the quality of circulation and differentiated subunit organization.
The bridge structure is insufficiently expressed, compromising architectural expression and credibility.
